title: China's suspension of its gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard-materials export ban to the US runs out (MOFCOM, Announcement 46 of 2024 Article 2)
source: NEWS: MOFCOM's November 2025 suspension of the dual-use export ban on gallium, germanium, antimony, superhard materials and graphite to the US 'until November 27, 2026' (Fastmarkets, Engineering News, The Star, all 2025-11; Mondaq/Clark Hill summaries 2025-11). Not found in any 2026-11-09 extension coverage read 2026-11-12: Reuters via The Star and political.org describe the six rare-earth announcements only, so whether this separate clock was rolled to 2027-01-10 with them is unknown. Filed estimate: press-reported, MOFCOM text not read.
notes: A SEPARATE CLOCK FROM THE 2027-01-10 ONE, 15 days out and so inside the horizon. The suspension covers Article 2 of Announcement 46 (2024), the US-specific ban on approving those dual-use exports; the three metals stay under licensing either way, and the ban on dual-use exports to US military users is untouched. China made roughly 99% of refined gallium and ~60% of refined germanium. Open question for the next pulse: was it extended alongside the 11-09 package? Research only; an estimate widens caution and never licenses a position.
